teaser: He could not afford a model. So he bought a mirror, and used the back of an old canvas.
review_notes:
Painted on the reverse of The Potato Peeler (1885); dimensions 40.6 x 31.8 cm (Met).
Quote 'I purposely bought a good enough mirror to work from myself, for want of a model': letter to Theo, September 1889, wording varies.
'More than twenty' self-portraits in Paris: Met figure.
Only securely identified photographs of van Gogh show him at 13 and 19: check.
Dated summer 1887 by the Met.

lesson.text: How do you learn to paint faces when you cannot pay anyone to sit for you? In Paris in 1887, Vincent van Gogh found the cheapest answer there is. He bought a good mirror and hired himself.

He was 34 and had been in the city for about a year, living with his brother Theo. Money was short. He painted himself more than twenty times in those two Paris years, not out of vanity but as practice, the way a musician plays scales.

Turn this painting over and you find another one. On the back is The Potato Peeler, a dark study of a peasant woman he had made in the Netherlands two years earlier. Canvas cost money, so he reused it.

The picture is small, about 41 by 32 centimeters (16 by 12.5 inches), barely bigger than a sheet of letter paper. In many places the brown canvas shows between the strokes. He was not polishing a portrait. He was testing something he had just discovered.

In Paris he had met the newest painters, who built pictures out of separate dots and dashes of pure color instead of blending them smoothly. Van Gogh tried their method and quickly bent it. His dashes are long and each group runs in its own direction.
Watch where the strokes are heading.

spots.title: The hat
spots.text: Long curved strokes of yellow, with a few green ones, follow the weave of the straw around the crown and brim. The brush does the job of the straw itself.

spots.title: The beard
spots.text: Short orange and red strokes fan out from the mouth and chin, bristling like real hair. Yellow lights on the cheek blend straight into it.

spots.title: The smock
spots.text: On the blue work smock the dashes fall in loose diagonals, mixed with green and pale yellow. It is the kind of jacket a laborer wore, not a gentleman's suit.

spots.title: The background
spots.text: Behind him, strokes of blue-gray and orange swirl around the head in rings, like ripples around a stone. An empty wall has become a field of energy.

lesson.text: Hat, hair, cloth, air: four textures, made only by changing the direction of the brush. A year later this would become the way he painted everything, from wheat fields to night skies. Here you see him working it out on his own face.
In van Gogh's hands, the direction of a brushstroke describes what a thing is made of. He practiced that language on himself first.

Color gets the same treatment. Yellow hat against a bluish violet wall, orange beard against a blue smock: he places opposites side by side so that each looks stronger. Almost nothing here is neutral. Almost.
One patch on this portrait is nearly pure white. Where?

spots.title: The collar
spots.text: A wedge of white shirt sits right under the beard. It is the calmest spot in the picture, and it works like a pause: next to it, the orange of the beard looks hotter and the blue of the smock cooler.

lesson.text: And the face itself? The green eyes look past the mirror, wary, a little tired. The straw hat was what he wore to paint outdoors, so this is how he wanted to be seen: a working painter, dressed for the job.
Almost everything we know about van Gogh's adult face comes from paintings like this one. The only photographs securely identified as him were taken when he was 13 and 19.

quiz.question: Why did van Gogh paint so many self-portraits in Paris?
options: He was commissioned by a gallery
He could not afford models and needed practice
quiz.explanation: He bought a mirror and used himself as a free model.

quiz.question: What is on the back of this canvas?
options: A painting of a peasant woman peeling potatoes
quiz.explanation: He reused a canvas that already carried The Potato Peeler.

quiz.question: What mainly creates the different textures of hat, beard and smock?
options: Real straw glued to the canvas
The changing direction of the brushstrokes
quiz.explanation: Each material gets strokes running in its own direction.

quiz.question: Which colors does he set against each other?
options: Opposites, such as yellow and violet, orange and blue
quiz.explanation: He pairs opposite colors so each looks stronger.

facts.text: This self-portrait is a large canvas, taller than a person.
facts.explanation: It is only about 41 by 32 centimeters.

facts.text: The background strokes swirl around the head in rings.
facts.explanation: The blue-gray and orange dashes circle the figure like ripples.

facts.text: Many photographs of the adult van Gogh survive.
facts.explanation: The only securely identified photographs show him at 13 and 19.
